statement: 5.5 Other separations Finally, let us briefly discuss seperations between our proof systems and some well-known further proof systems. In [6] it was shown that Cutting Planes does not p-simulate OBDD(∧), and by extension all OBDD-based proof systems. This clearly also holds for all of our proof systems. Furthermore, in [2] it was shown that Cutting Planes with unary coefficients is simulated by OBDD(∧, w), though to our knowledge it is unknown whether any OBDD-based proof system simulates the general version of Cutting Planes. All of these separations can be easily extended to our SDD/d-SDNNF-based proof systems without further issues.

In [6] it was shown that Cutting Planes does not p-simulate OBDD(∧), and by extension all OBDD-based proof systems. This clearly also holds for all of our proof systems. All of these separations can be easily extended to our SDD/d-SDNNF-based proof systems without further issues. Frege systems are also often considered in relation to OBDD-based systems. It is wellknown that OBDD(∧, w) is incomparable to bounded-depth Frege [14]. However, we leave it is an open question, whether the methods developed in [14] can be extended to SDDs and d-SDNNFs as well. Surprisingly, it has not been studied to our knowledge whether (unbounded depth) Frege simulates OBDD(∧, w). We also leave this question, as well as its extension to SDDs and d-SDNNFs open. 6 Conclusion

In [6] it was shown that Cutting Planes does not p-simulate OBDD(∧), and by extension all OBDD-based proof systems. This clearly also holds for all of our proof systems. Furthermore, in [2] it was shown that Cutting Planes with unary coefficients is simulated by OBDD(∧, w), though to our knowledge it is unknown whether any OBDD-based proof system simulates the general version of Cutting Planes. All of these separations can be easily extended to our SDD/d-SDNNF-based proof systems without further issues. Frege systems are also often considered in relation to OBDD-based systems. It is wellknown that OBDD(∧, w) is incomparable to bounded-depth Frege [14]. However, we leave it is an open question, whether the methods developed in [14] can be extended to SDDs and d-SDNNFs as well. Surprisingly, it has not been studied to our knowledge whether (unbounded depth) Frege simulates OBDD(∧, w). We also leave this question, as well as its extension to SDDs and d-SDNNFs open. 6 Conclusion Despite its versatility, the lifting method introduced in this paper is not strong enough for some purposes. Notably, even though an exponential separation between OBDDs and SDDs exists in the satisfiable setting [3], we are not aware of an exponential separation that can be encoded as a (k, log n)-CNF. Therefore, a proper exponential separation between OBDD(∧, r) and SDD(∧) would require more sophisticated methods. The same holds for any separations between proof systems using SDDs and those using d-SDNNFs, as even though there are known superpolynomial separations between the two representation formats in the satisfiable setting [20], it is unclear, whether these separations can be extended to the unsatisfiable setting as well. Furthermore, as a result of Lemma 23, our lifting method is completely defeated by resolution, and therefore by any proof systems using weakening. Thus it remains open, whether OBDD(∧, w) p-simulates SDD(∧, w) or even SDD(∧).

context: 6 Conclusion Despite its versatility, the lifting method introduced in this paper is not strong enough for some purposes. Notably, even though an exponential separation between OBDDs and SDDs exists in the satisfiable setting [3], we are not aware of an exponential separation that can be encoded as a (k, log n)-CNF. Therefore, a proper exponential separation between OBDD(∧, r) and SDD(∧) would require more sophisticated methods. The same holds for any separations between proof systems using SDDs and those using d-SDNNFs, as even though there are known superpolynomial separations between the two representation formats in the satisfiable setting [20], it is unclear, whether these separations can be extended to the unsatisfiable setting as well. Furthermore, as a result of Lemma 23, our lifting method is completely defeated by resolution, and therefore by any proof systems using weakening. Thus it remains open, whether OBDD(∧, w) p-simulates SDD(∧, w) or even SDD(∧). Another open problem concerns the one-shot restructuring rule (r) for SDDs and d- SDNNFs: it is currently open whether SDD(∧, w, r) and d-SDNNF(∧, w, r) are polynomially verifiable proof systems, as it is open whether the equivalence problem for SDDs/d-SDNNFs respecting different vtrees is polynomial-time verifiable, which is a problem that might also be of independent interest. Finally, we reiterate the long standing open problem of superpolynomial lower bounds for OBDD(∧, w, r), which are a necessary requirement for separating OBDD(∧, w, r) from d-SDNNF(∧, w, r).

statement: To define the new proof systems SDD(∧, r, w) and d-SDNNF(∧, r, w) as well as their restrictions, we literally only have to replace “OBDD” by “SDD” or “d-SDNNF” and “order ≤” by “vtree (T, b)” in the definition above. However, we need to carefully check whether they actually produce polynomially verifiable proofs! In particular, to the best of our knowledge it is not known whether the reordering rule stated as above is polynomially verifiable for SDDs or d-SDNNFs. To be more precise, given two SDDs D1 , D2 with vtrees (T1 , b1 ) ̸= (T2 , b2 ) it is unknown whether there exists a polynomial-time algorithm verifying whether fD1 = fD2 and the same holds for d-SDNNFs. Before discussing this further, let’s verify that the all other properties are fulfilled.
context: Dℓ that represents fDℓ = ⊥ where each line (Di , ≤i ) is derived according to one of the following rules: init fDi = fCj for some clause Cj in φ. join (∧) There are j, j ′ < i such that ≤i = ≤j = ≤j ′ and fDi = fDj ∧ fDj ′ . reordering (r) There is a j < i such that fDi = fDj (but ≤i ̸= ≤j ). −1 −1 weakening (w) There is a j < i such that ≤i = ≤j and fD j (1) ⊆ fD i (1). It is well known that all derivation rules can be verified in polynomial time (see [21]). We use the common convention and denote by OBDD(∧, r), OBDD(∧, w), and OBDD(∧) the subsystem that use only the stated derivation rules. Note that OBDD(∧) is already a sound and complete proof system for UNSAT. To define the new proof systems SDD(∧, r, w) and d-SDNNF(∧, r, w) as well as their restrictions, we literally only have to replace “OBDD” by “SDD” or “d-SDNNF” and “order ≤” by “vtree (T, b)” in the definition above. However, we need to carefully check whether they actually produce polynomially verifiable proofs! In particular, to the best of our knowledge it is not known whether the reordering rule stated as above is polynomially verifiable for SDDs or d-SDNNFs. To be more precise, given two SDDs D1 , D2 with vtrees (T1 , b1 ) ̸= (T2 , b2 ) it is unknown whether there exists a polynomial-time algorithm verifying whether fD1 = fD2 and the same holds for d-SDNNFs. Before discussing this further, let’s verify that the all other properties are fulfilled. ▶ Lemma 5. The following properties hold for d-SDNNFs and hence, for SDDs. 1. Given a circuit D and a vtree (T, b) it can be verified in polynomial time whether D is an d-SDNNF that respects (T, b). 2. Given d-SDNNFs D1 , D2 , D3 that respect the same vtree, it can be checked in polynomial time whether fD1 ∧ fD2 = fD3 . 3. Given d-SDNNFs D1 , D2 that respect the same vtree, it can be checked in polynomial time −1 −1 whether fD 1 (1) ⊆ fD2 (1). 4. Given a d-SDNNFs D, it can be checked in polynomial time whether fD = ⊥. A proof for Lemma 5 can be found in the full version. ▶ Corollary 6. SDD(∧), SDD(∧, w), d-SDNNF(∧), and d-SDNNF(∧, w) are sound and complete propositional proof systems. It turns out that without weakening, reordering steps can be verified in polynomial time.1 ▶ Lemma 7. SDD(∧, r) and d-SDNNF(∧, r) are sound and complete propositional proof systems.
